title: Introduce credential-snooze and stream-scheduler to harmonize auth backoff & streaming ergonomics across SDKs
author: Asha Kapoor
body: Motivation: Cross-language customers reported noisy token refresh churn when transient 401/429 windows occur concurrently with high-volume streaming usage. SDK teams implemented different local mitigations (varying backoff windows, uncoordinated reauth attempts, and ad-hoc stream retries) which produced inconsistent UX across Python/TS/Go, and led to duplicated load spikes against the control plane. This PR introduces two complementary primitives: (1) credential-snooze — a small, explicit window that pauses proactive credential refresh attempts after an auth failure to avoid repeated simultaneous refresh storms; and (2) stream-scheduler — a lightweight, opt-in cross-SDK coordinator that spaces out resubscribe/reauth attempts and surfaces typed lifecycle events to application code. Goals: reduce refresh storm frequency, unify streaming event shapes across SDKs, give devs a clear ergonomic surface to react to transient auth/backoff events, and bump SDKs to versions that include these primitives. What changed (high level): - Core: add credential-snooze policy implementation in the auth library with customizable windows and an adaptive decay (snooze_half_life) to auto-shrink snooze after success. - Stream scheduling: a small scheduler used by streaming transports that provides jittered retry slots and an event emitter API (streaming:ready, streaming:auth_snooze, streaming:backoff, streaming:resume). The emitter is typed in TS/Go and documented in Python examples. - SDK bindings: Py/TS/Go SDKs now expose optional Config.credential_snooze and Client.stream_scheduler options; opting out retains previous behavior. - Telemetry: expose cred_snooze.metrics (snooze_count, avg_snooze_ms) and stream_scheduler.metrics (slot_wait_ms, queued_resubscribe). - Tests & docs: unit + integration tests for coordinated reauth windows; new quickstart in redwood-quickstarts showing cross-sdk patterns. - Version bumps: py 1.13.0, ts 2.9.0, go v1.10.2. Compatibility: default behavior is backward-compatible. If users pass explicit credential refresh hooks with custom semantics they can still opt out by setting credential_snooze.enabled=false. Rollout plan: toggle on in Hosted for a small percentage, run Canary Dedicated with telemetry hooks, then fully enable as SDKs ship. Risk & mitigation: snooze windows can delay valid token refresh; we added conservative defaults (1000ms base with exponential decay capped) and a fast-path that bypasses snooze for explicit force-refresh calls. Implementation notes: see commit list below and inline doc updates.

review_thread: Diego Marin: Can we make the snooze window configurable per-credential? In some enterprise flows refreshes are multi-step and may need a longer snooze. — Requested changes
Asha Kapoor: Added per-credential override, kept global defaults conservative. See sdks/*/auth config additions. — Addressed

Lena Cho: Typing question: TS emitter payloads should use discriminated unions rather than loose any. Also add a tiny example showing how to pause application-level resubscribe until streaming:ready. — Requested changes
Asha Kapoor: Updated TS emitter types to use discriminated unions and added example in examples/credentials-snooze.md. — Addressed
Samir Patel: CI flake on go integration: the scheduler jitter seeds differed on arm runners causing a flaky assertion. Suggest we make the test tolerant to ±50ms. — Comment
Asha Kapoor: Adjusted test tolerance and seeded RNG for deterministic CI on linux-amd64 but kept arm non-deterministic guard. — Addressed
Diego Marin: Approve after behavior verification in staging (observed 72% reduction in near-simultaneous refresh attempts during burst workload). — Approved
Lena Cho: Approve. Nice ergonomics and docs. — Approved
benchmarks_summary: Sanity run: credential storm scenario (100 concurrent streams with intermittent 401s) showed a median 68% drop in concurrent refresh attempts and 35% reduction in 99th percentile resubscribe latency due to staggered retry slots. No meaningful increase in steady-state token fetch latency observed.
release_notes: Introduce credential-snooze and stream-scheduler. Default-enabled with conservative windows. SDKs: Python 1.13.0, TypeScript 2.9.0, Go v1.10.2. Adds telemetry (cred_snooze.* and stream_scheduler.*). Backwards compatible; opt-out supported.
